Determining Energy Requirements
Estimation of energy needs is difficult even in the healthy non-stressed individual, 
and becomes even more complex during illness and injury. Yet an accurate estimate 
of energy needs is critical in order to avoid the complications associated with over- 
and underfeeding. Starvation, a compensatory survival mechanism, is marked by 
reduced metabolic rate and protein preservation.28 Stress and acute illness differ from 
starvation in the metabolic use of substrates associated with catabolism. The stress 
response is characterized by increased energy expenditure, protein catabolism to sup-
port gluconeogenesis (production of glucose from protein), and hyperglycemia 
related to catecholamine and glucocorticoid increase that outweighs an increase in 
hyperinsulinemia. A number of different methods and formulas have been derived to 
aid in determining energy expenditure and calorie needs for healing.2,29,30 One of the
